record.paper_title: A List of Problems on the Reverse Mathematics of Ramsey Theory on the Rado Graph and on Infinite, Finitely Branching Trees
record.original_question: For the Rado graph, does the rainbow Ramsey property for k-bounded colorings have the same reverse-mathematical strength as the rainbow Ramsey property for (k+1)-bounded colorings?

evidence.quote: (10) Does the rainbow Ramsey property for k-bounded colorings of the Rado graph have the same reverse math strength as for (k + 1)-bounded colorings?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let R denote the Rado graph, i.e., the unique (up to isomorphism) countable graph that is universal and ultrahomogeneous for finite graphs. For a finite induced subgraph C of R and a positive integer k, a coloring c of the set of induced copies of C in R is called k-bounded if for every color, the preimage has size at most k. The Rainbow Ramsey property RR_k(R,C) states: for every k-bounded coloring c of the copies of C in R, there exists an induced subgraph R' ⊆ R isomorphic to R such that c is injective on the copies of C contained in R' (i.e., R' contains a "rainbow" copy structure). Let RR_k(R) abbreviate the statement "RR_k(R,C) holds for every finite induced subgraph C of R."

Working in the framework of reverse mathematics over the base system RCA₀, for each fixed integer k ≥ 1, determine whether the principle RR_k(R) and the principle RR_{k+1}(R) have the same reverse-mathematical strength; equivalently, decide whether RR_{k+1}(R) implies RR_k(R) and vice versa over RCA₀ (or relative to a suitable base theory sufficient to formalize the Rado graph).
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears in a 2018 problem list on the reverse mathematics of Ramsey theory on the Rado graph. Searches did not locate any follow-up work establishing or refuting the equivalence of k-bounded and (k+1)-bounded rainbow Ramsey principles for the Rado graph in reverse mathematics; related results address the rainbow Ramsey theorem for pairs of integers, not the Rado graph case. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Rainbow Ramsey Simple Structures
status_evidence.snippet: Defines rainbow Ramsey for ultrahomogeneous structures like the Rado graph with k-bounded colorings.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the framework of k-bounded rainbow Ramsey but does not resolve the reverse-math comparison.

status_evidence.title: The Strength of the Rainbow Ramsey Theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Reverse-mathematical study of rainbow Ramsey for pairs of integers.
status_evidence.claim: Related reverse-mathematics work, but on integers rather than the Rado graph.
